subject: Teeth
hook: TEETH IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Teeth are not made of bone, but actually evolved as modified fish scales. Mammal teeth still rely on the same developmental genes and tissues that built ancient fish scales.
angle_support: Teeth are not made of bone, but rather of multiple tissues of varying density and hardness that originate from the outermost embryonic germ layer, the ectoderm.

Study of a tooth plate of a fossil of the extinct fish Romundina stellina showed that the teeth and scales were made of the same tissues, also found in mammal teeth, lending support to the theory that teeth evolved as a modification of scales.
title: Why Your Teeth Are Actually Repurposed Fish Scales
description: While commonly mistaken for exposed bones, teeth originated through a completely different evolutionary path. Fossil evidence reveals that teeth share developmental genes and structural tissues with ancient fish skin scales that folded into the jaw over time.
narration: TEETH IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture them as exposed parts of your skeleton, hard white bones anchored inside your jaw. But teeth are not bone at all. They are actually ancient armored scales. Fossils of the early fish Romundina reveal that external scales and teeth shared the exact same tissues. In fact, our teeth still rely on the homologous developmental genes that originally built skin scales on ancient fish. Every bite you take uses modified prehistoric armor folded into your mouth.
